text:
sam: opened PR to update Nightingale-7B model card + migration notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4350. tl;dr: fix two broken bench links, clarify variant naming, add streaming SDK snippet for async client, and replace hard-coded external weights URL with a provenance block.

jordan: preview looks good overall. i did a quick scan: examples mix 'Nightingale-7B', 'nightingale7b', and 'nightingale_7b' in different places. we should pick the Catalog display name and add an explicit 'aliases' list so customers know accepted names.

mina: linkcheck flagged /assets/bench/nightingale/throughput.csv and an external weights path on storage.redwood.ai. infra guidance is to keep bench CSVs in docs repo and remove direct weight downloads from docs (provenance paragraph instead).

infra-bot: linkcheck: 2 broken links found (docs/model-sources.md#L22, /assets/bench/nightingale/throughput.csv). Recommendation: copy bench assets to docs/assets/bench/nightingale and replace absolute weight URLs with provenance link to upstream.

sam: i'll move the CSV into docs/assets/bench/nightingale and flip the links in the PR. ETA today EOD.

ava: small bench methodology nit: the throughput table didn't specify sequence length or batch-window. can we add a short "measurement methodology" subsection listing seq_len=1024, batch=4, batch_window=200ms and the exact runner args? saves back-and-forth with support.

jordan: also the benchmark numbers were collected before we enabled the quant-fallback path; we should either rerun with quant-fallback enabled or add a note explaining the difference. i'd prefer a footnote for now.

mina: SDK snippet currently shows a sync client with older response shape. i'll replace it with an async streaming example that demonstrates function/tool-like streaming and how to handle incremental chunks. example suggestion: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
async for chunk in client.generate_stream(model="nightingale-7b", prompt="Write a haiku about compilers"):
    print(chunk, end="")
```

sam: love the streaming example. please include a short comment showing how to fall back to a smaller variant if timeout/latency > SLO.

ava: migration guide note: customers pinned variant strings like 'nightingale7b-int8' without hyphen; runtime accepts aliases but config tools sometimes expect hyphenated form. add YAML example showing both: ```yaml
routes:
  - model: Nightingale-7B
    aliases: [nightingale7b, nightingale-7b-int8]
    pinned_variant: nightingale7b-int8
```

jordan: added a small wording change to clarify that the alias list is for convenience and the API resolves aliases to canonical runtime names. left a tiny nit about pluralization in the provenance sentence.

infra-bot: deploy-preview built. linkcheck: 1 broken link remains: https://storage.redwood.ai/models/nightingale/weights.tar.gz referenced from docs/model-sources.md.

sam: i'll remove the absolute weights URL from model-sources.md and point readers to the provenance block in the card (which links to upstream repo + license).

mina: pushed the streaming SDK snippet and a non-streaming async example. left a short TODO to add error-handling patterns for partial streams in a follow-up.

ava: moved throughput.csv into docs/assets/bench/nightingale and updated the table source. also added the methodology subsection with seq_len=1024 and batch_window=200ms.

doc-bot: CI passed. linkcheck clean. preview: https://deployments.preview.redwood.ai/docs/nightingale-7b-card

sam: merging shortly. thanks all for the quick reviews — this should reduce a bunch of support confusion. i'll open a tiny follow-up to add a lint check that warns when cards reference external storage URLs.

jordan: nice. will cross-post a short note to model-onboarding reminding folks to populate the aliases field in the template.

mina: thanks team. follow-up: i'll add a short example in the SDK guide showing resumable streams for large outputs.

sam: closing thread after merge. :white_check_mark:
